title: Async embeddings client: incremental cursor with deterministic ordering and graceful schema evolution
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Deliver a backwards-compatible async cursor for the Embeddings SDKs (Python + TypeScript) that provides: deterministic ordering of batched results for reranking workflows, idempotent resume tokens, strong error contract for transient vs permanent failures, and a clear schema evolution path for typed responses. This ticket covers API design, SDK implementations, server-side endpoint compatibility, test harness, and staged rollout guidance. Goal is to reduce re-ranking flakiness, improve latency for large batched queries, and make client retries safe for at-least-once upstream semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
Python and TypeScript SDKs expose an async Cursor/Iterator API that supports resume(token) and stable ordering guarantees.
    - resume token is opaque, idempotent, and valid across minor service restarts.
Deterministic ordering: identical input batch order must produce identical output order across retries (modulo documented stable tie-breaker behavior).
Typed responses: SDK responses are strongly typed (pydantic dataclass for Python, TS interfaces for JS) with explicit schema version v2 and a compatibility shim for v1 responses.

Pagination + streaming: large embedding requests can be consumed incrementally with bounded memory and predictable latency; test harness demonstrates <20ms median per-row latency bump for streamed batches vs previous blocking fetch under representative workload.
Retry semantics: transient errors (503, network) are safe to retry without duplication in reranking pipelines; permanent errors surface typed error classes to caller.
Server backwards compatibility: server accepts v1 and v2 client tokens; migration plan documented in rollout notes.
End-to-end tests: integration CI covers resume after network interrupt, resume after server rolling restart, and cross-language consistency checks (Python vs TS).
Telemetry: added metrics for resumed_cursor_count, stale_token_rate, and average_resume_latency; dashboards updated.
Docs: SDK docs pages for Python/TS with code samples for large-scale rerank loop, and migration guide from existing pagination APIs.
technical_notes: - Cursor token format: opaque base64 JSON that contains stream_id, sequence_offset, schema_version, and a cryptographic HMAC. Server validates HMAC to avoid accepting tampered tokens.

- Deterministic ordering: server returns elements in canonical sort order deterministic by input index and stable model scoring tie-breaker. Client preserves order; SDK exposes both ordered() and by_score() helpers.
- Schema evolution: v2 adds typed metadata (embedding_source, quantization_hint). SDKs implement a compatibility shim that maps v1 -> v2 with warnings.
- Error taxonomy: define TransientError, PermanentError, TokenExpiredError, PartialResponseError; map HTTP codes to these classes in both SDKs.
- Streaming performance: use chunked HTTP + JSONL frames for TS; Python uses streaming parsing with zero-copy where possible (memoryview) to reduce GC overhead.
- Backpressure: SDK exposes async buffer_size and max_concurrent_prefetch settings; default conservative values chosen based on benchmark.
- Accept and emit resume tokens v2; validate token HMAC; implement per-stream monotonic offsets.
- Add small server-side lookup cache to validate old tokens and map to new stream ids for a 48-hour window to facilitate in-flight resumes during rollout.
- Token leakage risk: HMAC prevents client forging; token TTL limited to 7 days and logged; we will add KMS rotation note in security review.
- Ordering guarantees add slight CPU to server sort; mitigated by only applying deterministic tie-breaker when client requests ordered-preserve flag.
- Local microbench: streaming parsing reduces end-to-end per-row CPU by ~12% (Python) and ~9% (TS) compared to previous blocking fetch.
- Load bench: replayed 10k rerank jobs showed resume token success rate 99.6% after simulated restarts.
implementation_plan: 1) API design doc + proto sketch (2 days) - attach and review.
2) Server-side token v2 support + HMAC validation (3 days) - implement and unit test.
3) Python SDK iterator + typed models (4 days) - pydantic models, streaming parser, retry mapping.
4) TypeScript SDK iterator + types (4 days) - TS interfaces, JSONL streaming helper.
5) End-to-end integration tests & stress bench (3 days).
6) Docs, migration guide, and rollout plan (2 days).
7) Staged rollout: beta with opt-in flag -> gradual default for 2 weeks -> full default and telemetry alerting.
testing_plan: Add unit tests for token generation/validation and schema version parsing.
Integration test that simulates network interrupt at random offsets and asserts resume correctness.
Cross-language consistency test: feed same seed inputs to Python and TS SDKs, assert identical ordering/typed fields.
Load test: 50k concurrent small embed requests with 100k resume operations over 48h window.
Chaos test: rolling restart of 3/5 server fleet while clients resume streams.
rollout_notes: Beta gate controlled by header X-Embeddings-Cursor: v2; default remains v1 initially.
Telemetry checks: if stale_token_rate > 0.5% for 24h during beta, revert and investigate.
Customer communication: targeted message to top rerank customers with migration guide & SDK patch notes.
Flag removal window: 2 weeks after hitting stability thresholds, flip default and increase token TTL to 7 days.
dashboards: embed-error-triage: TransientError rate, TokenExpiredError rate, PartialResponseError rate
